title: Quirks registry entry
description: One entry of specs/quirks/*.yaml (README.md). D20 (execution plan §2.6.3, SPEC-REG-QUIRKS) adds `affects` (the vendor versions an entry affects, rule 1), the lifecycle status `retired` (rule 4), `mapping` (what a hub does to a stored document, recorded per rule 3) and declaration entries (`applies_to: declarations`, rule 2). Every member D20 adds is optional; entries without them keep their project-level attribution. Checked by tools/nsschema/quirks.py at load.

status.description: Rule 4. `proposed`: suspected, not yet measured. `active`: measured in the corpus. `historical`: no recent write and no live instance of an affected version. `retired`: also no stored record depends on its mapping. Each move is measured by `make schema-quirks`; `make schema-quirks-check` fails a `historical` or `retired` claim the measurement does not support.

applies_to.description: Rule 1. `documents` (the default): stored documents, measured over the corpus by `detect`. `declarations`: a registration's slot names, units or vocabulary, mapped by the well-known catalogue for the affected versions and measured by a hub's recorded mappings.

affects.description: Rule 1: the (vendor, product, versions) this entry affects. `vendor` and `product` are a registration's `metadata.vendor` and `metadata.product`.

mapping.description: What a hub does to a document this entry describes, recorded on the stored record as `quirksApplied` (rule 3). `erasesEvidence`: the stored form no longer shows the quirk, so the corpus cannot count recent writes and only the hub's records measure the lifecycle.

declaration.description: For `applies_to: declarations`: the declared member and value the entry maps, for the affected versions. The catalogue publishes the mapping as a `wellKnown.mappings[]` entry of the capability document.

versions.description: A range over the vendor's own version strings (`*`, or whitespace-separated comparators `=`, `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` that must all hold; dot-separated parts compare numerically, numbers before text), stated only where the corpus or source shows it; otherwise `unmeasured`, saying why. `seen`: versions the evidence shows, which are not a range.

versionSource.description: Where `make schema-quirks` reads a version: `path` in the same document when `collection` is the entry's, else in the nearest `collection` document of the same site within `window_minutes` (co-occurrence, not attribution).
